editorial:
Imagine growing up in a giant, crumbling house in Pennsylvania with a father who acts more like a scary drill sergeant than a dad. That is exactly what Josie and Jack deal with. Since they were kids, they have been homeschooled and kept away from the rest of the world, meaning they only have each other to lean on. The movie takes you back to the 90s, giving you a real sense of that era. It feels very intimate and emotional, focusing on the tight bond between two siblings who are just trying to survive their father's strict rules and harsh personality. You will feel for them immediately as they try to find a way to be happy despite their lonely upbringing.

The acting is the best part here because you can really feel the love and tension between the lead actors. The story moves at a steady pace, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you prefer non-stop action. It is a touching story about family and breaking free. If you are in the mood for a heartfelt drama, you should definitely check it out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the details of that old mansion.
endingExplained: In the end, Josie and Jack finally break away from their father's control. They realize that their bond is stronger than the fear their father used to keep them trapped. After years of struggle, they find the courage to leave the house and start their own lives. The movie wraps up with them finding peace and independence, showing that they can survive and thrive once they are finally free from their toxic home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family bonds and overcoming hard childhoods.
